question: Should OpenClaw adopt this experiment-gated core CLI and `openclaw.clawUpdatePlan.v1` contract as the authoritative consent boundary for grouped Claw updates?
rationale: Implementation review can establish that the planner is coherent and read-only, but it cannot decide whether the open RFC's new core lifecycle, CLI, ownership, and compatibility contracts should become supported product behavior.

options.title: Approve and land in order
options.body: Accept the planner contract, merge its prerequisite first, and then land this slice before the apply executor.

options.title: Narrow the public contract
options.body: Keep the internal read-only planner but defer or reduce the CLI and versioned output commitments until the RFC is accepted.

options.title: Pause the Claws stack
options.body: Keep the implementation drafts unmerged while maintainers decide whether the broader lifecycle belongs in core.

recommendation.title: Approve and land in order
recommendation.body: Accept the planner contract, merge its prerequisite first, and then land this slice before the apply executor.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned reviewer and strongest visible owner of the agent-centric product and ownership model reflected in this planner.
